text.en:
A pothole appeared on Ravi's street. His father said, "The panchayat looks after village roads, but a highway belongs to the state or the Centre."
Ravi wondered how many levels of government there were.

India has three levels of government: local (panchayat or municipality), state and central (Union). Each does different work. The local government looks after streets, water and cleanliness. The state looks after matters such as police and farming. The Union looks after defence, currency and foreign affairs.
Every government has three organs. The legislature makes laws, for example Parliament and state assemblies. The executive carries them out, for example the Prime Minister, ministers and officers. The judiciary, the courts, settles disputes and checks that laws follow the Constitution.
Citizens take part by voting, paying taxes honestly, following laws and raising problems through the right channels.
India has local, state and central governments.
The executive carries out the laws.
The judiciary settles disputes and protects the Constitution.

problem.en: Who does what when a new law is made and used?

text.en: The executive puts it into practice.
If there is a dispute, the judiciary decides.

prompt.en: A friend says the government is only the Prime Minister. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: There are three levels of government.
There are three organs of government.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking one person is the whole government.

points.en: Citizens take part by voting and following laws.
